final.answer: GV-12-3 is described as a Type 165 2/2-way solenoid valve, so yes, it needs electrical power. The documentation lists available supply voltages of 24V DC, 230V AC 50/60Hz, and 115V AC 50/60Hz, with a voltage tolerance of ±10%. So 24 V DC will work — you do not need 230 V AC; either is acceptable depending on which coil variant is fitted. Note power consumption is 5 W (DC) or about 20 VA inrush / 11 VA (5 W) holding for AC, connection is via a cable plug (IP65), and you should match the voltage/current type marked on the type plate.

final.answer: The item directly upstream of BV-10-1 is TV-10-2, a globe valve whose datasheet is a Fisher ET. A Fisher ET is a complete control valve, not just the valve body — the datasheet describes it as a single-port, globe-style control valve with cage guiding, a balanced valve plug, and push-down-to-close action, consisting of the body plus trim, bonnet and other parts. It is a globe-style (globe-type) control valve, used for throttling or on-off control of a wide variety of liquids and gases. (Its related variants are the EAT angle-body version and the ETR push-down-to-open version.)
